subject: Aperture Medical — export-eligibility & pricing exception
messages:
From: Susan Tan <susan.tan@aperturemed.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 12 Nov 2026 09:15:00 -0500
Subject: Pilot contract / deployment + compliance questions

Hi Vanessa,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — the latency on embeddings was impressive. Procurement and security have a couple of hard constraints before we can sign a PoC: we need confirmation that (1) the model and data transfer will not leave our VPC for the PoC (on-prem or VPC-hosted), (2) Redwood will provide SOC2 evidence and an export-control attestation for AI-model inputs/outputs, and (3) we require a commercial concession given our NPI-sensitive workload.

Our vendor team is asking for an initial pricing adjustment (40% off list for the 6-week PoC) to justify the internal effort. I realize that’s out of your standard playbook, but if Redwood can support a short-term discount and the VPC deployment, we can move quickly to an internal sign-off and PO. I attached a short KYC package and the procurement checklist.

Can we get your quick assessment on eligibility for a private deployment and any export-control limitations?

Thanks,
Susan
Procurement Lead
Aperture Medical
Attachment: Aperture_KYC-Pack.zip (archive)

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Susan Tan <susan.tan@aperturemed.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 12 Nov 2026 11:02:00 -05:00
Subject: Re: Pilot contract / deployment + compliance questions

Hi Susan — really appreciate the fast follow. Looping in Laura from Deal Desk for the SOC2/KYC path and to validate any eligibility flags; I'll also bring Markus (head of sales) into pricing conversations.

Quick answers:
- We can offer a VPC-hosted Private deployment for a PoC, but export-control eligibility depends on the content (technical specs) and destination; Laura will start the intake.
- We typically cap first-time PoC discounts at 25% via standard playbook; anything deeper requires an exception and exec sign-off.

Laura — I uploaded Aperture's KYC package to the shared Drive link below. Can you confirm if medical devices / NPI processing triggers additional export or sanctions checks?

Markus — Aperture is asking for 40% for a 6-week PoC; request your guidance on escalation cadence if Deal Desk flags eligibility.

Thanks — V

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>

Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 13 Nov 2026 08:30:00 -05:00
Subject: Re: Pilot contract / deployment + compliance questions

Vanessa / Markus — I completed a triage of Aperture's KYC packet and procurement checklist. Summary:
- Company: Aperture Medical (US-incorporated; operations in US/EU).
- Documents received: corporate registry, two officer IDs, and an initial SOC-2 summary (attestation pending).
- Risk note: Aperture develops embedded medical device firmware; because the PoC will process clinical telemetry, we need an export-control review for potential EAR/ITAR applicability and confirm no sanctioned-country components.

Action items:
1) Rishi, legal: please confirm if we can proceed with a VPC-hosted PoC under current model licensing without a technical export-control exception. I suspect we can, but we may need a narrow contractual clause limiting use for clinical diagnosis and an audit right.
2) Commercial: if we mark this as "restricted-industry" for contract language, any discount above 30% requires VP approval.

I attached a short intake doc (Aperture_SAAS-Regs-Summary.docx).

Laura
Deal Desk — Redwood Inference
Attachment: Aperture_SAAS-Regs-Summary.docx (docx)

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 14 Nov 2026 16:45:00 -05:00
Subject: Re: Pilot contract / deployment + compliance questions

Team — legal read: Aperture's use case (processing firmware telemetry tied to medical devices) raises two considerations: export-control classification and allowed use under our standard commercial terms.

Recommendations:
- Eligibility: Proceed with a VPC-hosted PoC (data isolated) provided Aperture signs supplemental export-control addendum restricting model weights export and prohibits use for regulated clinical decision-making. Also require an annual compliance attestation from Aperture.
- Contract language: include a 6-month audit clause, explicit limitations on clinical diagnosis, and a termination-for-compliance-breach clause.
- Pricing: we should not approve a 40% discount without exec approval. A one-time initial concession up to 25% could be approved by Sales VP for acquisition; anything >25% requires SVP approval (e.g., Evelyn).

If Sales wants to pursue 40% to close this account quickly, legal will need an explicit exec sign-off on both the pricing exception and the compliance-risk acceptance.

Rishi
Counsel, Redwood Inference

From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 15 Nov 2026 09:10:00 -05:00
Subject: Re: Pilot contract / deployment + compliance questions

Thanks for the summaries. My position: we are willing to offer a one-time 25% PoC concession contingent on the export-control addendum and the audit clause Rishi proposed. That hits our acquisition threshold and keeps legal mitigations intact.

If Vanessa believes Aperture's strategic value justifies 40% (and the team is comfortable accepting the incremental compliance risk), escalate to Evelyn for final sign-off. Evelyn — can you confirm whether we should make an exception for this account? If yes, please include any non-standard SLA/commercial guardrails you want attached.

Markus
Head of Sales — Redwood Inference
